newsitem.title: UK: INSIGHT-Copper seeks direction, may test support.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT-Copper seeks direction, may test support.

text.p: 3 MONTH CLOSE * SUPPORT * RESIST * RSI14 * MA10 * MA30
---------------VIEWS FROM THE MARKET - April 18 ---------------
More sideways activity is expected on Friday between $2,245 and $2,290 a tonne, with the possibility of a test of the lower end, traders and analysts said.
The same picture was expected in aluminium, with a convincing dip below $1,550 sending prices to test the year's lows at $1,534, they added.
COPPER -
More consolidation, with a downside bias, was expected on Friday.

"The market has closed on support at $2,260 but below the 100-day moving average at $2,261, whilst the 10-day moving average is effectively capping the price upside we feel that there remains more scope to retest the downside at $2,245," broker Brandeis said.
The market was watching the outcome of the threated strike at Escondida on Friday, but management has said that output would not be affected. The strike was not seen as a major factor.
The charts, which had an inside day on Thursday, saw the 14-day RSI also moving sideways at 39 at Thursday's close, up one point from the previous day.
Below $2,245 support, the next level was pegged at $2,220, then $2,200.
At 0802 GMT three months LME copper was quoted at $2,272/77, up $2/$3 from Thursday's late close.
ALUMINIUM -
The market was also consolidating, and would likely continue to see lacklustre activity.
But some players were not ruling out a test of $1,550, which would send prices down to take a look at $1,534, the year's low.
"It should continue to drift lower and test support in the $1,530/35 area," broker Gerald said.
Analyst Martin Squires of Rudolf Wolff agreed the market was looking soft.
"The technical picture remains weak, as we expect further consolidation, though with a downward bias," he said.
At 0802 GMT three months aluminium was quoted at $1,551/53, up $1 from Thursday's late close.
--Eric Onstad, London Newsroom +44 171 542-8065
